chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about tasbīḥ in the place of relieving oneself and about reciting the Qur'an.
It has not been permitted in the lavatory to recite more than Āyat al-Kursī, or that one praise Allah, or the verse: “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

key_terms.آيَةِ الْكُرْسِيِّ: the well-known Qur'anic verse of the Throne
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: glorification of Allah through devotional remembrance
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: a Qur'anic phrase of praise meaning all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds

ai.seo_question: What may be recited in the lavatory according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the etiquette of dhikr and Qur'an recitation in the lavatory. It indicates restriction in such a place, allowing no more than Āyat al-Kursī or brief praise of Allah, including the words “الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ.”
